title: Caffeine drawer: oncall scratch + temporary procedures
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratch for the late shift. Not an official runbook — copy things into Confluence if we keep them. Use this when handing off to the next oncall so they have immediate context and the fastest-known mitigations.

Summary (top-line):
- 02:10 UTC: transient spike in request latency for model-serve-prod (p99 ~ 4.2s). Autocool triggered and scaled GPUs up 1 node.
- 02:24 UTC: traffic dropped back, but a persistent small error rate (~0.3% 500s) remains for the /v1/generate endpoint targeting gptx-13b-quant.
- 03:05 UTC: applied temporary routing policy to divert 10% of traffic to gptx-13b-fallback which reduced error rate to ~0.05%.
- Current action: still routing 10% to fallback; monitoring for regression.

Quick checks (first 5 things I run):
- kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=model-serve-prod -o wide  <-- pod status + node
- kubectl -n serving logs deploy/model-serve-prod -c runtime --since=15m | tail -n 200 <-- recent runtime errors
- grafana: infra/serving/model-serve-prod (p99 latency, 5xx rate, GPU mem)
- curl -s -X POST $TESTGEN --data '{"prompt":"ping"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY' -v <-- quick request to reproduce
- pd query incident --active --service "model-serve"  <-- check active PD incidents

Observed patterns + notes:
- The 500s appear to be TimeoutExceptions inside the kernel selection layer when sequence-length spikes. Happened once last week (INF-2784) and we had a suspected probe/large-batch request from an internal job.
- Autoscale does a warm-up that can cause a brief tail of errors while KV cache warms up; warmup is ~45–90s for cold-started nodes currently.
- Our circuit-breaker rule for quantized models is slightly stricter; fallback works but increases cost by ~8%.

Temporary mitigations applied (what I changed):
1) Routing tweak: set route weight for gptx-13b-quant -> 90%, gptx-13b-fallback -> 10% (policy id: route-2026-032).
   - CLI: rctl route update --id route-2026-032 --weights '{"gptx-13b-quant":0.9,"gptx-13b-fallback":0.1}'
2) Disable aggressive batching for incoming requests with seq_len > 1024 for 30m window (to avoid big batch creation).
   - Temporary config push: /configs/serving-runtime/batching/disable-big-batches-30m
3) Increased KV cache retention window on nodes being added to cluster to 180s (was 90s) to reduce cold misses during warmup.

Who to escalate to (order):
- On-call SRE lead: Jonas Lee (pager)
- Runtime engineer (kernel selection): Priya Menon (Slack @priya)
- Platform infra: Ravi Shah (if nodes failing to join)
- Product / Customer Success: Ashley Kim (for customer-facing comms if we open an incident page)

Customer impact:
- No active customer-facing page created yet; single customer (acme-corp) reported a failure at 02:12 UTC via in-app error logs (ticket INF-3031). Their requests were routed to fallback and succeeded but with increased latency. Consider contacting them if we widen routing.

Playbook snippets to copy into formal runbook (if we keep them):
- Reproduce: curl to TESTGEN as above with a 2048 token prompt; observe if p99 > 3s and 5xx > 0.2%
- Rollback routing: rctl route update --id route-2026-032 --weights '{"gptx-13b-quant":1.0}'
- Promote fallback: rctl route update --id route-2026-032 --weights '{"gptx-13b-quant":0.7,"gptx-13b-fallback":0.3}' (for brief periods)
- Node health: kubectl describe pod <pod> | grep -E "OOMKilled|CrashLoopBackOff"

Known gaps / TODOs for next person:
- Investigate job pattern that may send high seq_len batches — correlate with internal batch jobs (ticketed INF-2784 follow-up).
- Add a temporary synthetic that hits /v1/generate with variable seq_len to exercise kernel selector in staging.
- Consider lowering strictness of circuit-breaker for quantized models during peak windows. Needs perf sign-off.

Short-term experiment notes (ideas):
- Try pre-warming tiny KV cache on new nodes from a replica of hot_prefixes table so warmup behaves like 15–30s instead of 45–90s. Needs infra change and a config toggle.
- Add a rate-limiter for internal batch jobs that submit multi-request stacks to avoid creating huge batch windows.

Questions for the morning handoff:
- Did the fallback maintain success rate after 03:30? (I left the route at 10% until further notice.)
- Any changes to scheduled batch jobs between 01:30–02:30? (Check airflow and internal-job logs.)
- Did acme-corp require a postmortem or a status update?

Useful quick commands (copy/paste):
- Check model runtime pods: kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=model-serve-prod -o wide
- Tail runtime logs: kubectl -n serving logs deploy/model-serve-prod -c runtime --since=10m | grep -i "TimeoutException" | tail -n 50
- Update route weights: rctl route update --id route-2026-032 --weights '{"gptx-13b-quant":0.9,"gptx-13b-fallback":0.1}'
- Restart a pod (if stuck join): kubectl -n serving rollout restart deployment/model-serve-prod

Notes to next oncall:
- If you escalate to runtime, paste the log block around the first TimeoutException (02:09–02:16 UTC). They want the call stack + kernel id.
- If the error rate creeps above 0.5% for >10m, open an incident page and ping Ashley for customer comms.
- If nodes are flapping join attempt errors, don't scale down; pause autoscale by setting min-replicas to current for 20m while debugging.

End-of-shift handoff checklist (please update status on Slack #sre-oncall):
- [ ] Confirm 5xx < 0.2% for sustained 20m
- [ ] Confirm grafana alerts back to green
- [ ] Post a short note summarizing what was changed and whether the fallback is still active
- [ ] Copy any reproducible steps into Confluence under infra/playbooks/model-serve

Random notes / brain-dump (keep or delete):
- Observed one docker image pull throttling event on node eu-west-1a at 01:58 — might be unrelated but worth noting.
- We should add a synthetic that runs a 3-second sequence length ramp test every hour on canary pool.

-- Maya
(leave this doc as the quick scratch; if you turn it into a polished runbook, rename and move to shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/playbooks)
